title: Refactor terraform module for GPU node orchestration in Private (ASG + Karpenter unified)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a single Terraform module that can provision and manage GPU-backed node groups for Redwood Private deployments supporting both ASG-based nodegroups and Karpenter autoscaling. The module should include upgrade and maintenance primitives (rolling upgrades, AMI drivers lifecycle hooks), node/instance health checks, and wired-in observability hooks so Console can show node-level readiness and GPU health. It must be opinionated enough to enforce best-practices (cordon+drain hooks, graceful termination, driver DaemonSet vs baked AMI handling) but flexible via variables to support customer constraints.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Module creates GPU nodegroup in target VPC with either ASG or Karpenter path selectable by variable 'provisioner_type'.
2) Supports a 'driver_strategy' variable: 'daemonset' | 'baked-ami' | 'hybrid' and exposes clear lifecycle for upgrades.
3) Rolling upgrade flow: canary nodegroup creation, traffic migration via node affinity labels, full drain+terminate cycle with health gating.
4) Health checks: node readiness + custom GPU-health probe exported as cloud metric. Alerts and Console hooks available.
5) Terraform examples and automated terratest coverage exist.
6) Migration guide from current per-cluster scripts to module provided.
implementation_notes:
Architecture: the module is composed of three main submodules (compute, lifecycle, observability).
Compute: supports 'aws_asg' path (launch template + mixed instances policy) and 'karpenter' path (provisioner CR + node template).
Lifecycle: includes lifecycle hooks for ASG (lifecycle-hook -> lambda to drain + annotate), and Karpenter webhooks (pod eviction through graceful draining). We will add an optional SSM parameter/AMI tag to trigger driver bake flows.
Driver management: default to GPU driver DaemonSet (nvidia/gpu-driver-manager) for faster upgrades; for customers requiring hardened AMIs allow 'baked-ami' with preinstalled proprietary drivers. The 'hybrid' strategy uses DaemonSet for minor updates and AMI for major kernel-driver changes.
Health checks: node-exporter + custom GPU exporter that reports 'gpu_ready' boolean. Terraform wires up a CloudWatch metric filter and CloudWatch alarm resource. Console integration path adds tags/annotations for nodegroup.
Compatibility matrix: CUDA 11.8+, NVIDIA driver 525+, AMI families: ubuntu-22.04, alinux2-gpu. Documented in module README.
design_decisions_and_tradeoffs:
1) Single module vs separate modules: choose single module to reduce duplication and enable consistent lifecycle hooks across ASG and Karpenter, at the cost of more branching logic in the Terraform code.
2) DaemonSet vs baked AMI for drivers: DaemonSet chosen as default for faster iteration and safer rollbacks; baked AMI supported for customers with stricter cert requirements.
3) Canary approach: will prefer creating an isolated canary nodegroup so runtime traffic is migrated explicitly (safer) rather than in-place rolling updates which risk scheduling pressure. This increases short-term capacity cost during upgrade.
4) Observability: exporting GPU health as a metric is required for SLOs but increases cost from metrics; we will sample at 30s for nodes in 'upgrading' state and 60s otherwise.
test_plan:
Unit: terraform validate + tflint + checkov.
Integration: terratest harness that creates a small cluster in CI on a dedicated sandbox account and exercises provisioning in both 'asg' and 'karpenter' modes.
Upgrade tests: simulate driver upgrades with DaemonSet rolling update, and AMI bake + ASG replace. Verify node readiness, pod disruption budgets, and GPU metrics.
E2E: deploy a simple GPU workload (torch inference container) and assert successful scheduling before/after upgrade.
Load tests: run synthetic inference load to detect scheduling/backpressure regressions.
Nightly regression job: runs subset of tests in sandbox.
rollback_plan:
1) If canary shows failures, stop rollout and revert deployment by keeping old node group active and draining new nodes.
2) For DaemonSet driver rollbacks, use kubectl rollout undo on the DaemonSet through automation.
3) For AMI-based upgrades, revert ASG launch template to previous AMI ID and trigger instance refresh rollback.
4) For Karpenter, adjust provisioner constraints to reject new nodes and let existing nodes serve until fixed.
All rollback operations must be guard-railed by an automation runbook and notified via #infrastructure-alerts channel.
migration_steps:
1) Run 'terraform plan' against existing cluster with 'preview=true' to surface delta.
2) Create a canary nodegroup using the module in 'asg' mode and migrate low-risk workloads.
3) Validate GPU metrics and readiness for 48 hours.
4) Gradually increase traffic and scale down legacy groups.
5) Once stable, decommission legacy provisioning scripts and flip default variables to point to module outputs.
Provide a one-page migration playbook in Confluence.
